We all listen to various kinds of music, from post-rock to happy hardcore, on a daily basis. While I have a large library, I realize from time to time that I could use some more artists and bands to be exposed to.

So my question for you is this: What is your favorite genre and one song/album/compilation which can represent that genre best? It would be nice to see folks writing down why they think that one song/album/compilation does represents the genre the best or at least shows the genre has to offer.

One my favorite genres is Goa Trance, a sub-group of Trance music. Without going all into all the history and details of Goa Trance, it is well known for being melodic, acid sounds, weird sound effects, voice samples from space/science/drug cultures, and ultimately the large amount of variety. The last part is what makes it very difficult to choose one album that represents the genre because of how large range of different styles and atmospheres that exist in this genre, from melancholic to super energetic sounds.

But ultimately, I chose 12 Dimensions by Radical Distortion. This Israeli group has been part of the scene for quite some time. They first started out with some more nitzho stuff (in other words, energetic/happy/etc). But over the years, they have been developing their sound and their music productions more and more. Though they are a modern Goa Trance group, they used analog synthesizers and other hardware gear, as opposed to using soft-synths/etc, when making this album. That's one of the reasons why I chose this album because though they are making modern Goa, they are using methods that may be seen as older, vintage, archaic by some when we have the blessings of modern technology that allows us to all of it on a computer.

The other reason why I chose this album is because of the content within it. Though it may not represent all of what Goa Trance has to offer, it sure does a good job at showcasing what it does have. One thing is the nature of the album/tracks. They aren't really super energetic (in a happy, summer beach way) but aren't too dark either. It sort of sits in the middle between the two. Another thing is the compositions, sounds, etc of the tracks. While they are modern and are influenced by the current evolution of the genre, they still retain that old school nature and sound that the 90s Goa had.

In short, while it may not represent every aspect of the genre, this album does an excellent job at being a great Goa album.
